lesson_title: A Bill Is a Claim, Not a Command: Creditors Reconciliation
hook_text: Their bill says R59 250. Your book says R40 440. Pay the wrong one and you lose R13 850.
clip_script: You run a spaza. Every week you fetch stock from the wholesaler and write in your exercise book what you took and what you paid. Month end, they post you a bill: you owe us R59 250. Your book says R40 440. Do you just pay their number? That is somebody else's book about your money. Do you refuse and insist on yours? Your book has holes too. So you sit down with both and go line by line — and the differences are only ever three kinds. Things that are late: an invoice still in the post, a payment they have not banked. Things you never knew about: interest for paying late, a discount for paying early, nobody phoned you either time. And things that are simply wrong — because unlike a bank charge, the wholesaler's clerk is a person, and people put one customer's delivery on another customer's account. Fix what is yours: plus R6 400, minus R1 260, plus R620, minus R800. Forty-five thousand four hundred. That is what you honestly owe. The rest is theirs to fix. A supplier's bill is a claim, not a command.
visual_style: A spaza counter at dusk: a printed wholesaler statement on one side, a worn exercise book on the other, matching lines lighting up green and mismatches flaring amber until both totals settle on R45 400.
pacing: Punchy opening comparison, rhythmic line-by-line sort, firm closing rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and reconcile the statement yourself — line by line, before you pay a cent.
